title: Display the number of notifications on the systray instead of the bell when applet is always visible
line: The Notifications icon now shows the number of unread notifications in a small badge on the bell.
explanation: When there are unread notifications, the compact representation only swapped the bell for the ringing-bell icon, which at panel size looks almost identical to the idle bell, so people who keep the icon always visible (or need a larger, clearer cue) easily miss new notifications. The count label that used to exist is only shown for running jobs. The change adds the shared workspace BadgeOverlay (the same badge the keyboard layout tray icon uses) at the bell's bottom-right corner, visible only in the unread state, so it hides during Do Not Disturb and job progress.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: show the unread count in a badge on the icon

With unread notifications the icon only switched to a ringing bell that
looks almost the same as the idle one, which is easy to miss when the
icon is always shown. Now a badge with the count appears on the bell.

BUG: 432045

From 3b288821276667c98b4cf787429798f85b124125 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Subject: [PATCH] applets/notifications: show the unread count in a badge on
 the icon

With unread notifications the icon only switched to a ringing bell that
looks almost the same as the idle one, which is easy to miss when the
icon is always shown. Now a badge with the count appears on the bell.

---
 applets/notifications/CompactRepresentation.qml | 11 +++++++++++
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+)

diff --git a/applets/notifications/CompactRepresentation.qml b/applets/notifications/CompactRepresentation.qml
index 16b47a3002..56fa9ac3a7 100644
--- a/applets/notifications/CompactRepresentation.qml
+++ b/applets/notifications/CompactRepresentation.qml
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@ import org.kde.plasma.components as PlasmaComponents3
 import org.kde.plasma.plasmoid
 import org.kde.kirigami as Kirigami
 import org.kde.quickcharts as Charts
+import org.kde.plasma.workspace.components as WorkspaceComponents
 
 import plasma.applet.org.kde.plasma.notifications as Notifications
 
@@ -94,6 +95,15 @@ MouseArea {
         }
     }
 
+    WorkspaceComponents.BadgeOverlay {
+        id: unreadBadge
+        anchors.bottom: notificationIcon.bottom
+        anchors.right: notificationIcon.right
+        horizontalPadding: Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing / 2
+        text: compactRoot.unreadCount
+        visible: false
+    }
+
     Kirigami.Icon {
         id: dndIcon
         anchors.fill: parent
@@ -129,6 +139,7 @@ MouseArea {
             when: compactRoot.unreadCount > 0
             PropertyChanges {
                 notificationIcon.source: "notification-active-symbolic"
+                unreadBadge.visible: true
                 // Needed so the Transition with the bell animation restores properly
                 // should the animation get interrupted by switching to do not disturb while it's running.
                 notificationIcon.rotation: 0

Same setup: the bell carries a badge with the unread count

reviews.text: Minimal, idiomatic QML change that reuses `WorkspaceComponents.BadgeOverlay` to display the unread notification count at the bottom-right corner of the bell icon during the `UNREAD` state. Placing the badge as a sibling of `notificationIcon` keeps it stationary during the bell swing animation, and tying its visibility to the `UNREAD` state ensures it hides properly during Do Not Disturb and active jobs. The before/after screenshots confirm the badge looks clean and addresses the usability/accessibility report in line with maintainer feedback.

The reporter couldn't tell the unread bell from the idle one and asked to see the number; Nate agreed and Kai (c5) accepted a number in a badge if it looks good. The patch reuses the shared WorkspaceComponents.BadgeOverlay (Kirigami.Badge) anchored to the bell's corner and shows it only through the existing UNREAD state, so it stays hidden during jobs (whose countLabel takes over) and Do Not Disturb, and comes back on its own. The screenshots show a clear '3' badge that doesn't break the bell, and the verify notes cover two-digit counts, clearing on open, and DND. Showing the badge in auto-hide mode too is consistent and needs no new setting.
